research_question: What is the effect of antifibrinolytic drugs (tranexamic acid, aminocaproic acid or similar), compared with placebo or open (no-drug) control, on intracerebral haematoma expansion by 24 hours in adults with acute spontaneous (non-traumatic) intracerebral haemorrhage?
outcome_description: Number of participants with intracerebral haematoma expansion (events) out of total randomised participants (intention-to-treat denominator) assessed on repeat brain imaging at or around 24 hours after baseline scan, using the trial's reported expansion criteria
positive_direction: Favours antifibrinolytic therapy (reduced risk of intracerebral haematoma expansion at 24 hours)
search_queries: tranexamic acid intracerebral hemorrhage hematoma expansion randomized trial
antifibrinolytic spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage hematoma growth controlled trial
tranexamic acid ICH repeat CT haematoma expansion comparison
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trials enrolling adult patients with acute spontaneous (non-traumatic) intracerebral haemorrhage
Comparison of an antifibrinolytic drug (such as tranexamic acid or aminocaproic acid) against placebo or open/usual care control
Reporting quantitative haematoma expansion incidence or counts on repeat brain neuroimaging at or around 24 hours post-baseline
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, protocols, and case series)

No randomised comparison between an antifibrinolytic agent and a placebo or open control (non-randomised studies, single-arm studies, or active comparators of other haemostatic agents such as rFVIIa, PCC, or platelet transfusion)
Traumatic intracranial haemorrhage, aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage, or non-spontaneous ICH populations without separable spontaneous ICH subgroup data
No quantitative dichotomous outcome data on haematoma expansion at or around 24 hours (e.g. reporting only mean volume change without patient counts, or only late 90-day clinical outcomes)
moderators_to_extract: Specific antifibrinolytic drug and dosage regimen
Time window from symptom onset to treatment randomisation/administration
Definition and criteria for haematoma expansion (e.g., relative >=33%, absolute >=6 mL, or composite)
Control type (placebo-controlled double-blind vs open-label usual care)
Mean or median baseline haematoma volume
effect_size_note: Risk ratio (RR) pooled using a random-effects model (DerSimonian-Laird or REML/PMA). An RR < 1 indicates a lower incidence of haematoma expansion in the antifibrinolytic arm (favours treatment). Event counts are taken from trial-defined expansion criteria on repeat scan at ~24 hours; denominators are the full intention-to-treat randomised sample size per arm. Multi-arm trials with multiple active antifibrinolytic dosing groups are combined into a single active arm by summing events and total randomised participants.
